title: Read the slope or intercept
subtitle: Linear equations in two variables · 16 official questions

sections.heading: Where this sits for you
body: **16 of the official questions in Linear equations in two variables are this one** — 5 Easy, 7 Medium, 4 Hard.
Most versions sit at the Medium tier.

sections.heading: How to spot it
body: You are looking at this pattern when:
- It's a short stem: 'what is the slope of the graph of…', 'what is the y-intercept of the line shown', or 'the y-intercept is (0, k), find k'.
- You're given a single equation, often in standard form, or a single graph.

sections.heading: The method
body: - 1) For the y-intercept, set x = 0 and solve for y (or read where the line crosses the y-axis).
- 2) For the slope, solve for y and take the coefficient of x (for Ax + By = C, it's -A/B).

sections.heading: Where Desmos fits
body: Type the equation and click where the line crosses the y-axis; Desmos labels the point.
For the slope, click two grid points on the line and compute rise over run.

sections.heading: What it is built to catch
body: You give the x-intercept instead of the y-intercept, give the whole ordered pair when a single coordinate is asked, or read the slope straight off standard form as A or B without dividing and changing the sign.

sections.heading: You are losing these
body: Before you choose, say out loud what the question is asking for — not what you solved for.
